assumptions: N=50 trim, chosen by the human at CONFIRM; save-on-main-only and leave-it were rejected

The trim is a separate verb (`canary history trim`), not a side effect of `history record` — proposal 460's append-only, unbounded write contract stays true for every consumer, and only the caller who asks for a bound gets one
50 sits above both read-side windows (flake minimum 10, analyze window 30), so a trimmed store can never starve a reader into an abstention that still exits 0
'Newest' means timestamp order, not append order — the same rule queryFlaky and querySummary already apply (#604)
Surviving rows are written back as their original bytes rather than re-serialized, so a field a newer canary wrote is not silently dropped by a retention operation
`trim` refuses when a db-url is configured rather than silently succeeding: an exit 0 over an untouched remote store would be a false green
